text:
maya_cs: Drafting a 1-page "lite" onboarding handout for mobile-first customers (tight token budgets + flaky networks). Goal: give engineers and PMs a tiny checklist + paste-ready snippets.

maya_cs: TL;DR checklist:
1) Prefill 2-3 starter messages server-side to reduce cold tokens.
2) Prefer small batches (2-4 inputs) or concatenated prompts for single-turn flows.
3) Use streaming only for interactive typing/UX.
4) Set a soft token alarm (alert 24h before quota) and a renewal_watch flag if sustained high burn.
5) Post-go-live: auto ping for 1-question feedback 1h after first production usage.

leo_se: tiny ask: include 1x curl batch example + 1-line streaming switch for our SDK so customers can copy/paste. also call out when concatenation is better vs batch arrays.

maya_cs: added. note on concat vs batch: concat when responses should see full prior context in one output (cheaper single output tokens). batch arrays when you want independent outputs in parallel.

maya_cs: ```
# batch (curl) - send a small group of independent prompts
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3.1-small","inputs":["Help me name this item","Summarize this note"],"max_tokens":120,"stream":false}'

# concat (single output) - cheaper if you need context stitched
# join messages on client: prompt = messages.join("\n---\n")

# SDK one-liner to switch to streaming (node pseudo):
await client.generate({model:'redwood-3.1-small', input:prompt, stream:true})
```

harper_sre: ops notes to include in handout:
- cache prefix TTL = 20s for mobile sessions.
- per-tenant concurrency limit = 2 by default (bump on request).
- warm pools: pre-warm 1 GPU shard for expected surge windows (5-10min before).
- fallback: if median latency > 400ms for 30s, auto-reduce `max_tokens` by 30% for mobile clients.

maya_cs: added SRE notes. also added health rule: set `renewal_watch` when daily avg token burn > 70% of monthly quota for 3 consecutive days OR DAU spike > 2x baseline + token burn +20%. When the flag is set create a CS ticket with reason + suggestions.

jamie_pm: outreach copy for CS to use when renewal_watch triggers (short + helpful):
"Hey <name> — we noticed your app's usage is increasing and you9re approaching your monthly budget. Can we help optimize prompts or enable short-term burst capacity while you ramp? Quick call or a few prompt tweaks often fixes it."

maya_cs: included that verbatim and attached link to the public playbook (short checklist) in the convo doc.

maya_cs: Feedback capture snippet (post-go-live, 1h after first production request):
```
# POST to customer's feedback webhook (example)
curl -X POST https://hooks.customer.com/redwood-feedback \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"<TENANT>","timestamp":"$NOW","nps":"0-10","comment":"one-line"}'

# we recommend asking a single question: "How useful was the response? (0-10)"
```

onboard_bot: created doc in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/lite-mobile-onboard (access: customer-success, product)

leo_se: nit: add example header `X-Client-Mode: mobile` and example of setting `typing=true` in the stream to render a typing indicator. small UX win.

maya_cs: good call, added header note + tiny UX best-practice: if streaming, send an initial 80-char prefix to get first tokens out faster; then stream remainder.

maya_cs: publishing plan: attach to low-touch kickoff template + include in onboarding email as "lite engineering checklist". please comment with edits by EOD, otherwise I'll publish. :rocket:
